questions.learningObjective: evaluate image resolution in a design critique
questions.stem: On Image resolution: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a low-resolution photo looks soft when printed at a large size. What does resolution describe in this situation?

options.text: The number of pixels available to reproduce the image detail
The total number of colors in the image's palette
options.misconception: confuses the pixel count with the color depth of the file

options.text: Only the physical dimensions of the printed page
options.misconception: ignores the pixel information in the image entirely

options.text: The overall brightness level of the reproduced image
options.misconception: mistakes tonal value for the density of image detail

questions.explanation: Resolution refers to the pixel information contained in an image. Too few pixels for a large print forces enlargement of each individual pixel, producing softness, so matching pixel dimensions to the output size preserves detail.
questions.hint: Is the underlying problem a count of pixels or a count of colors?
